irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Gated Optionality - the ability to model that a specific party (Required Facility Lenders) has the discretionary option to trigger a rule/condition
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The existing IF, COMPARE, AND/OR/NOT structures can express conditions but not the optionality layer that 'at the option of Party X' introduces. Currently, such optionality must be represented as a pure condition (treated as always available) or collapsed into a condition that presumes the party exercises the option. The distinction between 'a rule that applies when X occurs' and 'a rule that applies at the option of Party Y when X occurs' cannot be cleanly separated in the current IR without either losing the optionality signal or embedding it in free-text description.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: DISCRETIONARY_GATE or PARTY_OPTION_GATE: a new expression node kind that carries (a) the underlying condition/trigger expression, (b) the party with discretion, and (c) optionally a default behavior if the discretion is not exercised. This would allow clear representation of pricing step-ups, acceleration options, and similar optionality patterns that frequently appear in credit agreements.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Temporal Transition / Phase Shift Triggering - the ability to model that a rate/term changes on a specific operational date (delivery of first full fiscal quarter financials) independent of a calendar date
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The current SCHEDULE and AS_OF/DURING_PERIOD structures are designed for calendar-based or period-based transitions. The transition from Phase 1 to Phase 2 of Applicable Rate is triggered by a specific operational event (delivery of financials per Section 6.01), not by the passage of time or a specific calendar date. TRANSACTION_INPUT_REFERENCE is a proxy but not semantically accurate for a conditional state machine transition.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: EVENT_TRIGGERED_PHASE_SHIFT or OPERATIONAL_TRANSITION: a node that carries (a) the list of phase/stage expressions in order, (b) the trigger event for each transition (not a date but a business event like 'delivery of X' or 'satisfaction of condition Y'), and (c) how fallback/default phases are determined if a trigger event is not satisfied by an expected date. This would cleanly represent tiers of pricing that shift on regulatory filing, measurement cycles, or other operational events.

This compilation addresses two closely related defined terms from Section 1.01: 'Applicable Liquidity Threshold' and 'Applicable Rate', both fundamental to the credit agreement's operational mechanics.

APPLICABLE LIQUIDITY THRESHOLD: The definition establishes a base threshold of $37.5 million with a conditional increase mechanism. If the Super-Senior Revolving Facility's maximum committed amount increases beyond $62.0 million, the threshold is increased by 26% of the excess (RCF Increase Amount), capped at a maximum of $50.0 million. The logic is fully represented as MIN(base + conditional_increase, max_cap) using an IF expression to gate the increase calculation. However, the 'Super-Senior Revolving Facility' itself is not defined in the supplied evidence, resulting in PARTIAL sufficiency despite complete representation of the computable formula.

APPLICABLE RATE: This definition has two distinct phases: (1) initial period until delivery of first full fiscal quarter financials per Section 6.01, with static rates (8.00% Term Benchmark, 7.00% Base Rate), and (2) thereafter, variable rates based on a three-tier pricing schedule keyed to the Secured Net Leverage Ratio as measured in the most recent Compliance Certificate per Section 6.02(1). The three pricing levels are clearly defined with threshold ratios and corresponding rates for both Term Benchmark and Base Rate loans. The definition also includes two critical exceptions: (a) Required Facility Lenders may apply Pricing Level 1 when a Compliance Certificate delivery is late or missed (from first Business Day after the miss until certificate is delivered), and (b) at their option, apply Pricing Level 1 from first Business Day after an Event of Default under Section 8.01(1) until that default is cured or waived. All of this structure is represented, though with noted limitations around modeling 'party optionality' and 'operational event triggers' for phase transitions.

SUBORDINATE DEFINITION - RCF Increase Amount: The provision explicitly parenthetically defines 'RCF Increase Amount' as the excess of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility maximum committed amount over $62.0 million. This has been extracted as a separate definition (d2) for clarity and referenced by Applicable Liquidity Threshold. Its sufficiency is also PARTIAL due to the unresolved Super-Senior Revolving Facility reference.

INVENTORY ACCOUNTABILITY: Of the 39 inventory items provided, 26 pertain to Asset Sale exclusions and are not operative in the definitions being compiled here - these are marked INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL with a note that they belong to a separate Asset Sale definition section. The remaining 13 critical and material items are all consumed by the definitions and rule compiled: Applicable Liquidity Threshold condition and formula (3 items), Applicable Rate initial rates (2 items), subsequent rate based on leverage ratio (1 item), three pricing levels (3 items), rate adjustment trigger (1 item), and Event of Default pricing exception (1 item). One quantitative value detected deterministically ($37.5 million) participates in d1's material proposition and is consumed there.

CROSS-REFERENCES TO UNRESOLVED EXTERNAL PROVISIONS: The operative text references Section 6.01 (financial statement delivery timing), Section 6.02(1) (Compliance Certificate requirement), and Section 8.01(1) (Event of Default definition). These are captured in dependsOn relationships and the rule's own conditions and exceptions. Sections 7.01, 7.03, 7.05 referenced in Asset Sale are out of scope per the source context state.

DEFINED TERM DEPENDENCIES: Applicable Rate depends on 'Term Benchmark Loans', 'Base Rate Loans', and 'Secured Net Leverage Ratio', all resolved except that Term Benchmark Loans and Base Rate Loans have not been individually extracted as definition excerpts (they are references rather than calculations in the Applicable Rate definition itself). Applicable Liquidity Threshold depends on 'Super-Senior Revolving Facility' (unresolved) and 'Refinancing Indebtedness' (resolved).

EXTENSION CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED: Two genuine IR extension candidates emerged: (1) DISCRETIONARY_GATE or PARTY_OPTION_GATE to cleanly represent 'at the option of [party]' layering on top of a condition or rule, and (2) EVENT_TRIGGERED_PHASE_SHIFT to model operational state transitions (like moving from Phase 1 to Phase 2 Applicable Rate) driven by business events rather than calendar dates. Both appear in frequently in complex credit agreements and would improve the semantic fidelity of rate and pricing definitions.

MODELING NOTES: The Applicable Rate's two-phase structure was represented as a top-level IF distinguishing 'before first fiscal quarter financials' vs. 'thereafter', with the 'thereafter' branch containing a SCHEDULE of three pricing-level cases. This reflects the natural logic flow of the definition. The Event of Default exception in r1 references Section 8.01(1) and is structured as an exception to the general rule that pricing level changes effective per Compliance Certificate delivery. The 'at the option of Required Facility Lenders' constraint is noted in the condition description but not fully separated as a gating layer - this is a limitation of the current IR that the extension candidate would address.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Gated Optionality - the ability to model that a specific party (Required Facility Lenders) has the discretionary option to trigger a rule/condition
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The existing IF, COMPARE, AND/OR/NOT structures can express conditions but not the optionality layer that 'at the option of Party X' introduces. Currently, such optionality must be represented as a pure condition (treated as always available) or collapsed into a condition that presumes the party exercises the option. The distinction between 'a rule that applies when X occurs' and 'a rule that applies at the option of Party Y when X occurs' cannot be cleanly separated in the current IR without either losing the optionality signal or embedding it in free-text description.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: DISCRETIONARY_GATE or PARTY_OPTION_GATE: a new expression node kind that carries (a) the underlying condition/trigger expression, (b) the party with discretion, and (c) optionally a default behavior if the discretion is not exercised. This would allow clear representation of pricing step-ups, acceleration options, and similar optionality patterns that frequently appear in credit agreements.

irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Temporal Transition / Phase Shift Triggering - the ability to model that a rate/term changes on a specific operational date (delivery of first full fiscal quarter financials) independent of a calendar date
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: The current SCHEDULE and AS_OF/DURING_PERIOD structures are designed for calendar-based or period-based transitions. This would cleanly represent tiers of pricing that shift on regulatory filing, measurement cycles, or other operational events.

overallNotes: This compilation addresses two closely related defined terms from Section 1.01: 'Applicable Liquidity Threshold' and 'Applicable Rate', both fundamental to the credit agreement's operational mechanics.

APPLICABLE LIQUIDITY THRESHOLD: The definition establishes a base threshold of $37.5 million with a conditional increase mechanism. If the Super-Senior Revolving Facility's maximum committed amount increases beyond $62.0 million, the threshold is increased by 26% of the excess (RCF Increase Amount), capped at a maximum of $50.0 million. The logic is fully represented as MIN(base + conditional_increase, max_cap) using an IF expression to gate the increase calculation. However, the 'Super-Senior Revolving Facility' itself is not defined in the supplied evidence, resulting in PARTIAL sufficiency despite complete representation of the computable formula.

APPLICABLE RATE: This definition has two distinct phases: (1) initial period until delivery of first full fiscal quarter financials per Section 6.01, with static rates (8.00% Term Benchmark, 7.00% Base Rate), and (2) thereafter, variable rates based on a three-tier pricing schedule keyed to the Secured Net Leverage Ratio as measured in the most recent Compliance Certificate per Section 6.02(1). The three pricing levels are clearly defined with threshold ratios and corresponding rates for both Term Benchmark and Base Rate loans. The definition also includes two critical exceptions: (a) Required Facility Lenders may apply Pricing Level 1 when a Compliance Certificate delivery is late or missed (from first Business Day after the miss until certificate is delivered), and (b) at their option, apply Pricing Level 1 from first Business Day after an Event of Default under Section 8.01(1) until that default is cured or waived. All of this structure is represented, though with noted limitations around modeling 'party optionality' and 'operational event triggers' for phase transitions.

SUBORDINATE DEFINITION - RCF Increase Amount: The provision explicitly parenthetically defines 'RCF Increase Amount' as the excess of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility maximum committed amount over $62.0 million. This has been extracted as a separate definition (d2) for clarity and referenced by Applicable Liquidity Threshold. Its sufficiency is also PARTIAL due to the unresolved Super-Senior Revolving Facility reference.

INVENTORY ACCOUNTABILITY: Of the 39 inventory items provided, 26 pertain to Asset Sale exclusions and are not operative in the definitions being compiled here - these are marked INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL with a note that they belong to a separate Asset Sale definition section. The remaining 13 critical and material items are all consumed by the definitions and rule compiled: Applicable Liquidity Threshold condition and formula (3 items), Applicable Rate initial rates (2 items), subsequent rate based on leverage ratio (1 item), three pricing levels (3 items), rate adjustment trigger (1 item), and Event of Default pricing exception (1 item). One quantitative value detected deterministically ($37.5 million) participates in d1's material proposition and is consumed there.

CROSS-REFERENCES TO UNRESOLVED EXTERNAL PROVISIONS: The operative text references Section 6.01 (financial statement delivery timing), Section 6.02(1) (Compliance Certificate requirement), and Section 8.01(1) (Event of Default definition). These are captured in dependsOn relationships and the rule's own conditions and exceptions. Sections 7.01, 7.03, 7.05 referenced in Asset Sale are out of scope per the source context state.

DEFINED TERM DEPENDENCIES: Applicable Rate depends on 'Term Benchmark Loans', 'Base Rate Loans', and 'Secured Net Leverage Ratio', all resolved except that Term Benchmark Loans and Base Rate Loans have not been individually extracted as definition excerpts (they are references rather than calculations in the Applicable Rate definition itself). Applicable Liquidity Threshold depends on 'Super-Senior Revolving Facility' (unresolved) and 'Refinancing Indebtedness' (resolved).

EXTENSION CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED: Two genuine IR extension candidates emerged: (1) DISCRETIONARY_GATE or PARTY_OPTION_GATE to cleanly represent 'at the option of [party]' layering on top of a condition or rule, and (2) EVENT_TRIGGERED_PHASE_SHIFT to model operational state transitions (like moving from Phase 1 to Phase 2 Applicable Rate) driven by business events rather than calendar dates. Both appear in frequently in complex credit agreements and would improve the semantic fidelity of rate and pricing definitions.

MODELING NOTES: The Applicable Rate's two-phase structure was represented as a top-level IF distinguishing 'before first fiscal quarter financials' vs. 'thereafter', with the 'thereafter' branch containing a SCHEDULE of three pricing-level cases. This reflects the natural logic flow of the definition. The Event of Default exception in r1 references Section 8.01(1) and is structured as an exception to the general rule that pricing level changes effective per Compliance Certificate delivery. The 'at the option of Required Facility Lenders' constraint is noted in the condition description but not fully separated as a gating layer - this is a limitation of the current IR that the extension candidate would address.

findings.sourceEvidence: "Applicable Liquidity Threshold" means $37.5 million; provided that to the extent that, as of any date of determination, the maximum committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility (or any Refinancing Indebtedness in respect thereof) is increased in excess of $62.0 million (such excess amount, the "RCF Increase Amount"), the Applicable Liquidity Threshold shall be increased by an amount equal to 26.0% of the RCF Increase Amount up to a maximum Applicable Liquidity Threshold not to exceed $50.0 million.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR models Applicable Liquidity Threshold as MIN(ADD($37.5M, IF(RCF Increase Amount > 0, 26.0% × RCF Increase Amount, 0)), $50.0M). The IR represents the structure as: base amount plus a conditional increment, capped at $50.0M.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text states the threshold 'shall be increased by an amount equal to 26.0% of the RCF Increase Amount' only 'to the extent that...the maximum committed amount of the Super-Senior Revolving Facility...is increased in excess of $62.0 million'. The RCF Increase Amount is defined as the excess over $62.0M. The condition in the proposed IR—'IF(RCF Increase Amount > 0, ...)' —correctly triggers when the RCF Increase Amount exists. However, the proposed IR's structure of MIN(ADD(...), $50M) is accurate: the base is $37.5M, increased conditionally, with a hard ceiling of $50M. Upon careful re-reading, the proposed IR's logical structure—MIN(ADD(base, increment), cap)—does faithfully represent 'increased by...up to a maximum...not to exceed'. The use of IF to model the conditional trigger is appropriate because RCF Increase Amount only exists when the condition in the source is met. This is not a structural error.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR includes a 'defaultValue' field within the SCHEDULE expression for the Applicable Rate, marked as 'UNSUPPORTED' and described as: 'Fallback case when Secured Net Leverage Ratio does not match any of the three pricing levels.' findings.verifierReasoning: The source text defines exactly three pricing levels with three discrete ratio bands: (1) >1.00 to 1.00, (2) <1.00 to 1.00 and >0.50 to 1.00, (3) <0.50 to 1.00. These are mutually exclusive and exhaustive for all non-negative ratios; every possible non-negative ratio falls into exactly one of these three categories. There is no fourth level, and the source provides no guidance on what applies if a ratio falls outside these ranges (which is logically impossible given the ranges cover all positive values). The proposed IR correctly flags the defaultValue as UNSUPPORTED. This is not a defect in the IR marking; the IR's honest disclosure of unsupported structure is appropriate. However, a competent reviewer should verify that the three pricing levels truly do cover all possible ratio scenarios, which they do.

findings.sourceEvidence: The rule in the proposed IR relates to Pricing Level 1, which applies 'at the option of the Required Facility Lenders' under two scenarios: (x) failure to deliver a Compliance Certificate and (y) occurrence of an Event of Default. The source text states: 'at the option of the Required Facility Lenders, "Pricing Level 1" (as set forth above) shall apply as of (x)...and (y)...'.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed rule has posture 'N_A', action null, and capacityExpression null. The rule is structured entirely as a list of conditions and exceptions, with no core prohibition, permission, or obligation statement.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text describes when and under what conditions a lender may elect to apply Pricing Level 1. This is inherently a conditional rule of effect—it describes when a specific rate (and by extension, when lender economics) change. The rule has a clear logical structure: 'IF [scenario (x) OR scenario (y)], THEN Pricing Level 1 applies (at lenders' option).'
